entation Index\n> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.mcpjam.com/llms.txt\n> Use this file to discover all ava

# MCPJam API

> Programmatic access to the MCP servers in your MCPJam projects: diagno

stics, tool calls, prompt rendering, and asynchronous eval runs.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **The MCPJam API is in preview.** It works
today and we use it ourselves, but\n> it has not been generally announced and the surface may change, including in\n> breaking way
s, while we finish the design. Pin your integration to the\n> behaviors documented on this page, build a [tolerant\n> reader](#ver
sioning--stability), and expect to revisit it. Feedback is very\n> welcome on [Discord](https://discord.gg/JEnDtz8X6z) or\n> [GitH

ub](https://github.com/MCPJam/inspector/issues).

> [card] [Create an API key](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys)
>
> G
o straight to key management in the hosted app. If you're signed out,\n> you'll be asked to sign in and then land right back on th

e API keys page.

The MCPJam API lets you operate the MCP servers saved in your
[hosted](https://docs.mcpjam.com/hosted/overvie

w.md) projects (from CI, scripts, or your own agents)
without opening the UI.

What you can do with it today:

* **Discover y
our resources**: list your projects, their servers, eval\n suites, and chat sessions, so every ID the other routes need is\n sel
f-serve\n* **Validate a server**: connect, initialize, and capture a capability snapshot\n* **Run the doctor**: the probe → connec
t → initialize → capabilities workflow\n* **Check OAuth requirements**: does this server need an OAuth grant?\n* **List tools, pro
mpts, and resources**: the server's MCP primitives\n* **Call a tool / render a prompt**: execute primitives and get the MCP result

back verbatim
* **Read a resource** by URI
* **Export a full snapshot**: tools, resources, and prompts as one JSON document
*
**Manage a project's clients**: list, read, **create** (from a built-in\n template like `claude`/`chatgpt`/`cursor`, or from a fu
ll config), edit,\n duplicate, and delete the named, reusable configurations that define how\n MCPJam connects to and talks to y
our MCP servers. Edits are compare-and-set:\n read the client, then send its `configId` back as `expectedConfigId` for a\n confi
g change and its `name` back as `expectedName` for a rename (a rename\n does not rotate the config, so the config token cannot de
tect a concurrent\n one), and a concurrent edit is rejected rather than silently reverted\n* **Manage a project's environments**:
list, read, and archive the named\n execution bundles (host + optional server group) that eval\n suites and goals run against,\
n and **preview** what one resolves to before launching it\n* **List a project's studies**: name, access mode, attached servers,

and
 share link, and **read one study's settings**: model, system prompt,
 tool-approval policy, and resolved servers
* **Aut
hor eval suites**: create a runnable suite (name, default model, servers, test cases) synchronously and get a `suiteId` back; no r
un is started and no credits are spent\n* **Run eval suites asynchronously**: create a run from a saved suite, get a `202` + `runI
d`\n immediately, then poll status, per-iteration results (tool calls, token\n usage, latency), and full traces. Runs appear liv

e in the hosted UI,
 tagged `source: "api"`
* **Manage a server's accounts**: complete OAuth yourself (e.g. the SDK's
 `run
OAuthLogin`, or your CI's own sign-in) and upload the token to a named\n account; list, rename, choose the default, and delete ac

counts. Tokens are
 write-only: no route returns one
* **Run a headless agent turn**: send a message history, get back the
 a
ssistant reply, the platform operations it invoked, references to any\n resources it created (eval suites), and token usage; the

model is pinned
 server-side and billed to the project
* **Send feedback**: report a bug, a missing capability, or something

confusing to the MCPJam team at the moment you hit it; the same endpoint the
 `send_feedback` MCP tool calls

All endpoints o
perate on servers you have already added to a project in the\nhosted inspector. Managing API keys remains UI-only; see\n[Not in th

e API yet](#not-in-the-api-yet).

## Base URL

```text theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1
```

The API is path-versioned. All routes on this page are relative to the base
URL above.

## Authentication

Every request

needs an MCPJam API key in the `Authorization` header:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
curl -X POST \
 "https:
//app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/tools\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\" \\\n -

H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{}'
```

### Creating a key

1. Open [**Settings → API keys**](https://app.mcp

jam.com/settings/api-keys)
 in the hosted app (the card at the top of this page takes you there
 directly).
2. Click **Crea
te API key**, name it, and pick the **organization** it will act in.\n3. Copy the key (`sk_…`) immediately; **it is shown exactly

once** and never
 stored by MCPJam in retrievable form.

Keys can be revoked from the same page at any time. Revocation takes

effect
immediately.

### Scope

A key is bound to one MCPJam organization at creation and acts **as you,
inside that organi
zation**. Per-request authorization still applies: a call\nonly succeeds if the key's owner can access that project and server. A

key
can never reach projects outside its organization.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Two deliberate restrictions while in preview:
>
> * *
*API keys cannot manage API keys.** Requests to the key-management surface\n> with an `sk_…` bearer fail with `403 FORBIDDEN`. C

reate and revoke keys in
> the UI.
> * **Guest sessions cannot use the API.** Sign in to create keys.

### Keep keys secret\

n
Treat an API key like a password:

* Load it from an environment variable or secret manager; never commit it to
 source con
trol or ship it in client-side code.\n* Scope keys narrowly: one key per integration, named so you can tell them apart.\n* Rotate
by creating a replacement key, switching traffic, then revoking the old one.\n* If a key leaks, revoke it immediately in\n [**Set
tings → API keys**](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys).\n\nIf you see `401 UNAUTHORIZED` with `details.reason: \"ORPHANED_K
EY\"`, the key\nis no longer bound to an organization and cannot be used; create a new key\nfrom [Settings](https://app.mcpjam.com

/settings/api-keys).

## Conventions

**Requests.** Operations on servers are `POST` with a JSON body (most accept
an empty `
{}`). **Reads**, the catalog listings and eval-run polling, are\n`GET` and take their options (`cursor`, `limit`, filters) as quer

y
parameters.

**Responses.** Three envelope shapes, used consistently:

| Kind | Shape |
| - | - |
| Single resource | The
resource object directly |\n| Collection | `{ \"items\": [...], \"nextCursor\": \"...\" }`; `nextCursor` omitted on the last page

|
| Error | `{ "code": "...", "message": "...", "details": {...} }` with a matching HTTP status |

**Pagination.** C
ollections are cursor-based. Pass the previous response's\n`nextCursor` as `cursor` in the next request (body field on `POST` list

s,
query parameter on `GET` lists). Cursors are opaque; don't parse them.

**Authoring vs running suites.** `POST /eval-suites`
creates a runnable suite\n(the suite plus its test cases) **synchronously** and responds `201` with the\n`suiteId`, WITHOUT runni
ng anything; author once, run later. `POST /eval-runs`\nis the async counterpart: it validates and creates a run synchronously, th
en\ndetaches execution and responds `202` with a `runId`. Poll\n`GET /eval-runs/{runId}` until `status` is `completed`, `failed`,\

n`cancelled`, or `timed_out`.

**IDs.** Every identifier the API takes is discoverable through the API
itself: `GET /projects`
lists your projects, `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers`\nlists each project's servers, and `GET /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites
